current_example.problem: Solve the equation $5ky-13=7$ for the variable $y.$
current_example.worked_solution:
We need to isolate $y.$ To do this, we first add $13$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}5ky-13 & =7 \\ 5ky-13+13 & =7+13 \\ 5ky & =20\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide both sides of the equation by $5k\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}5ky & =20 \\ \frac{5ky}{5k} & =\frac{20}{5k} \\ \frac{\cancel{5k}y}{\cancel{5k}} & =\frac{20}{5k} \\ y & =\frac{20}{5k}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can further simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{5\cdot 4}{5k} \\ y & =\frac{\cancel{5}\cdot 4}{\cancel{5}k} \\ y & =\frac{4}{k}\end{aligned}
$$
